title: Charge Transfer and Conservation
learning_goal: Investigate conservation of charge during induction, conduction, and polarization.

stages.title: 1. Charge is conserved
stages.content: Electric charge can move from one object to another, but total charge is conserved. Electrons are transferred or rearranged; charge is not created or destroyed in ordinary electrostatic interactions.

stages.title: 2. Charging by conduction
stages.content: Conduction occurs when charged objects touch and electrons transfer through direct contact. After contact, the objects may share the same type of net charge.

stages.title: 3. Charging by induction
stages.content: Induction charges an object without direct contact. A nearby charged object causes charges to rearrange. With grounding, electrons can enter or leave, producing a net charge.

stages.title: 4. Polarization
stages.content: Polarization is the separation of positive and negative charge within a neutral object. The object remains neutral overall, but one side becomes slightly more positive and the other more negative.

stages.title: 5. Guided practice
stages.prompt: A negatively charged rod is brought near a neutral metal sphere without touching it. Electrons in the sphere move away from the rod. What process is occurring?
stages.hint: There is no contact, and charges inside the sphere are rearranging.
stages.alternate_explanation: The sphere stays neutral overall, but its charges separate because of the nearby rod.
stages.answer: Polarization, which is the first stage of induction.

stages.title: 6. Mastery check
stages.content: To demonstrate mastery, distinguish conduction, induction, and polarization, track electron movement, and explain how each process obeys conservation of charge.

concept_cards.title: What moves between ordinary solid objects during charging by rubbing?
concept_cards.content: Electrons can be transferred between materials. Protons remain bound in nuclei under ordinary charging conditions.

concept_cards.title: A neutral object gains electrons. What is its net charge?
concept_cards.content: Gaining negative carriers creates an excess of electrons relative to positive charge. Charge is conserved across the whole interacting system.
